message.content:
Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed for both food quality and service. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|-----------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, optional tofu) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Baan Thai** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Thai Orchid** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell peppers, bamboo shoots)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Siam Square** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup” (no shrimp, optional tofu) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | | **Thai House** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 226‑7777 | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants are located on the same block (1220 W 18th St), so you can easily walk between them if you want to try a few different dishes. They’re all in the West Loop, a vibrant neighborhood with plenty of other dining options. ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai Food 1. **Ask for “no egg” and “no fish sauce.”** Many Thai dishes contain egg or fish sauce by default. Requesting “no egg” and “no fish sauce” will make the dish vegetarian. 2. **Request tofu or tempeh.** Tofu is a common protein substitute in Thai cuisine. If you’re looking for a protein source, ask for tofu or tempeh in place of meat. 3. **Look for “vegetarian” or “vegan” labels.** Most of these restaurants have a dedicated vegetarian menu or at least a few vegetarian options clearly marked. 4. **Check the online menu.** Many restaurants post their menus on their website or on platforms like Yelp, Google Maps, or TripAdvisor. This can give you a quick overview of vegetarian options before you go. 5. **Call ahead if you have special dietary needs.** While most places are accommodating, it’s always a good idea to call and confirm that they can meet your specific requirements. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more detailed reviews, directions, or reservation help, just let me know.
